name: Aluminum 6061-T6
description: Widely used general-purpose aerospace and structural aluminum alloy with good weldability, corrosion resistance, and strength.

name: Aluminum 7075-T6
description: High-strength zinc-alloyed aluminum primarily used in aircraft airframes, spacecraft structures, and high-stress rocketry components.

name: Aluminum 2024-T3
description: High yield strength aluminum alloy with exceptional cyclic fatigue resistance, widely used in aircraft fuselage skins and tension members.

name: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5)
description: The workhorse titanium alloy of the aerospace industry, offering superb strength-to-weight ratio, fracture toughness, and corrosion immunity.

name: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Grade 23)
description: Extra-low interstitial purity version of Ti-6Al-4V engineered for cryogenic pressure vessels, medical implants, and fracture-critical space hardware.

name: Stainless Steel 304
description: Standard austenitic 18/8 stainless steel providing excellent ductility, corrosion resistance, and cryogenic toughness.

name: Stainless Steel 316L
description: Molybdenum-bearing austenitic stainless steel engineered for marine, chemical, and additive manufacturing space applications.

name: Stainless Steel 17-4 PH
description: Martensitic precipitation-hardening stainless steel combining high tensile strength, hardness, and moderate corrosion resistance.

name: Inconel 718
description: High-strength, corrosion-resistant nickel-chromium superalloy capable of withstanding extreme cryogenic to 700 °C temperatures in rocket turbopumps and hot gas manifolds.

name: Inconel 625
description: Solid-solution strengthened nickel-based superalloy delivering outstanding fatigue strength and oxidation resistance at elevated temperatures.

name: Oxygen-Free Electronic Copper (C10100)
description: Ultra-pure oxygen-free copper with exceptional electrical and thermal conductivity, utilized in rocket combustion chamber liners and heat sinks.

name: Beryllium Copper (C17200)
description: Highest strength copper-based alloy combining high electrical conductivity with mechanical strength exceeding many alloy steels.

name: Magnesium Alloy AZ31B-H24
description: Ultra-lightweight wrought magnesium alloy with good room-temperature strength, ductility, and vibration damping capacity.

name: Tungsten (Pure W)
description: Refractory metal with the highest melting point of all pure metals and exceptional resistance to high-temperature thermal creep.

name: Molybdenum (Pure Mo)
description: High-temperature refractory metal characterized by high elastic modulus, low thermal expansion, and high thermal conductivity.

name: Tantalum (Pure Ta)
description: Dense, ductile refractory metal with exceptional chemical inertness and immunity to acid attack, used in electronics and hot-gas propulsion.

name: Alloy Steel AISI 4140 (Chromoly)
description: Versatile chromium-molybdenum through-hardening steel known for high fatigue strength, toughness, and torsional rigidity in shafts and fasteners.

name: Low Carbon Steel AISI 1018
description: Standard free-machining low-carbon mild steel providing balanced machinability, weldability, and structural ductility.

name: Alumina Ceramic (Al2O3 99.5%)
description: Hard technical oxide ceramic with high dielectric strength, wear resistance, chemical inertness, and high-temperature stiffness.

name: Silicon Carbide (SiC - Sintered Alpha)
description: Extremely hard, abrasion-resistant covalent ceramic with high thermal conductivity and low thermal expansion, used in rocket nozzles and armor.

name: Silicon Nitride (Si3N4)
description: High fracture toughness engineering ceramic with exceptional thermal shock resistance, used in turbine blades and precision bearings.

name: Yttria-Stabilized Zirconia (3Y-TZP)
description: Transformation-toughened ceramic featuring low thermal conductivity and thermal expansion matched closely to cast iron, utilized in thermal barrier coatings (TBC).

name: Boron Carbide (B4C)
description: Known as 'black diamond', one of the hardest known materials with very low density, used in bulletproof armor and neutron absorber shielding.

name: Aluminum Nitride (AlN)
description: High thermal conductivity electrical insulator used for heat sinks in power electronics and semiconductor packaging.

name: Mullite Ceramic (3Al2O3·2SiO2)
description: High-temperature refractory silicate ceramic with superior thermal stability, low thermal expansion, and resistance to creep at >1400 °C.

name: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE / Teflon)
description: Fluoropolymer with unmatched chemical resistance, extremely low coefficient of friction, high electrical resistivity, and broad working temperatures (-200 °C to 260 °C).

name: Polyetheretherketone (PEEK - Unfilled)
description: High-performance semicrystalline engineering thermoplastic offering high mechanical stiffness, wear resistance, radiation stability, and low outgassing in vacuum.

name: Polycarbonate (PC / Lexan)
description: Amorphous engineering thermoplastic known for high impact resistance, optical clarity, dimensional stability, and flame retardancy.

name: Nylon 6/6 (Polyamide PA66)
description: Versatile engineering plastic offering high tensile strength, stiffness, abrasion resistance, and good tribological properties for gears and bearings.

name: Polyimide Film (Kapton HN)
description: Aromatic polyimide space film possessing outstanding thermal stability (-269 °C to 400 °C), dielectric strength, and UV radiation endurance for MLI blankets.

name: Ultra-High-Molecular-Weight Polyethylene (UHMW-PE)
description: Ultra-dense chain polyethylene with unmatched abrasion resistance, cryogenic impact resistance, self-lubrication, and zero moisture absorption.

name: High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE)
description: Lightweight, highly flexible, chemical-resistant polymer with high hydrogen density, making it effective for space radiation shielding.

name: Polypropylene (PP)
description: Lightweight thermoplastic polymer with excellent chemical resistance, fatigue resistance ('living hinges'), and low density.

name: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA / Acrylic)
description: Transparent thermoplastic with high optical transmission (92%), UV resistance, and moderate stiffness used in viewing ports and optical canopies.

name: Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS)
description: Tough, rigid terpolymer commonly used in prototyping, consumer electronics casings, and additive manufacturing.

name: Carbon Fiber Composite (CFRP - Unidirectional High-Modulus)
composition: Toray M40J Carbon Fiber (60% Vf) / Epoxy Matrix
description: Ultra-stiff lightweight aerospace composite providing extraordinary axial stiffness and near-zero axial thermal expansion for optical benches and satellite trusses.

name: Carbon Fiber Composite (CFRP - Quasi-Isotropic)
description: Balanced multi-directional carbon fiber composite delivering balanced planar stiffness, high specific strength, and vibration dampening for structural chassis.

name: Glass Fiber Composite (GFRP / E-Glass Epoxy)
description: Electrically non-conductive, high-strength structural composite with excellent radiofrequency (RF) transparency for antenna radomes and fairings.

name: Carbon-Carbon Composite (C/C)
composition: Carbon fibers in pyrolyzed carbon matrix
description: Ultra-high-temperature structural composite retaining full strength at temperatures >2000 °C in inert or vacuum atmospheres, used in rocket nozzles and nose cones.

name: Ceramic Matrix Composite (C/SiC)
composition: Carbon fibers embedded in Silicon Carbide matrix
description: Damage-tolerant ceramic composite combining high thermal shock resistance and oxidation resistance for atmospheric re-entry heat shields and brake rotors.

name: Borosilicate Glass (Pyrex / Borofloat 33)
description: Low-expansion optical and thermal glass with excellent thermal shock resistance and chemical durability for optical windows and vacuum sight ports.

name: Fused Silica (High Purity Synthetic Quartz Glass)
description: Non-crystalline amorphous silica with exceptionally low thermal expansion, high transmission from DUV to NIR, and extreme thermal shock tolerance.

name: Soda-Lime Float Glass
description: Prevalent window and substrate glass offering high planar smoothness, optical transparency, and low material cost.

name: Zerodur Glass-Ceramic
composition: Lithium aluminosilicate glass-ceramic (55% nanocrystalline quartz phase)
description: Zero-expansion glass-ceramic developed for space telescope primary mirrors (Hubble, JWST testbeds) with thermal expansion near zero over -50 °C to 100 °C.

name: Macor Machinable Glass-Ceramic
composition: Fluorophlogopite mica in borosilicate glass matrix
description: Machinable glass-ceramic that can be turned, milled, and drilled with standard metalworking tooling, with zero porosity and ultra-high dielectric strength.

name: Synthetic Diamond (CVD Polycrystalline)
description: Material with the highest thermal conductivity and hardness known, wide optical transparency, and chemical inertness for extreme laser optics and heat spreaders.

melting_point.notes: Under high pressure; graphitizes > 1700 °C in vacuum

name: Synthetic Graphite (Isotropic High-Density)
description: Self-lubricating, high-temperature thermal conductor that strengthens as temperature increases up to 2500 °C, used in rocket nozzles and nuclear moderators.

name: Silicon (Single Crystal Semiconductor Grade)
description: Elemental semiconductor forming the base of microelectronics, photovoltaic solar cells, and MEMS inertial sensors with extreme surface flatness.

name: Pure Iron (Alpha Ferrite)
description: Ferromagnetic elemental transition metal serving as the foundational constituent of carbon steels and superalloys.

name: Pure Nickel (Nickel 200)
description: Commercially pure nickel offering superior resistance to caustic alkalis and acids, good magnetostrictive properties, and electrical conductivity.

name: Space Shuttle TPS Tile (LI-900 Silica Tile)
composition: 99.9% High Purity Amorphous Silica (SiO2) Fibers (94% volume void)
description: Ultra-low-density sintered silica fiber thermal insulation tile developed by Lockheed and NASA Ames for the Space Shuttle orbiter re-entry heat shield.

name: Phenolic-Impregnated Carbon Ablator (PICA)
composition: Carbon Fiber Preform infused with Phenolic Resin
grade: NASA Ames PICA (Stardust / Mars 2020 / Dragon Heat Shield)
description: Lightweight carbon-phenolic ablative thermal protection system developed by NASA Ames for hyperbolic planetary entry missions and Crew Dragon heat shields.

name: Silica Aerogel (Hydrophobic Nanoporous)
description: Lowest density solid material with lowest thermal conductivity, used for Mars rover electronics bay insulation and Stardust cosmic dust capture.

name: Pure Gold (Au 99.99%)
description: Noble metal with exceptional infrared reflectivity, high thermal/electrical conductivity, and total oxidation immunity for satellite thermal mirrors and foil coatings.

name: Pure Silver (Ag 99.99%)
description: Highest electrical and thermal conductivity of all known elemental metals, with highest visible light reflectance.
